device.codeHint: This device's code. It is compared by voice or in person before the device is let into a conversation.

keys.title: Only you hold the keys
keys.text: Messages, files, reactions and calls are encrypted on the participants' devices. The server stores only ciphertext: it knows who wrote to whom and when, but not what.

devices.title: A new device
devices.text: Signed in on a new device? Approve it from your old one: both screens show the same emoji, compare them and press “Yes”. The device gets the keys and the history. Without that, the other person can let it in after comparing its device code with you.

recovery.title: The recovery key
recovery.text: Without your old device at hand, the recovery key brings the history back. Save it when the app asks: without it old messages are unavailable on a new device, and the server can't restore it.

safety.title: Checking who you talk to
safety.text: The shield in the conversation header opens the safety code. Compare it with the other person in person or over another channel and mark “Codes match” — the shield turns green. If they add a new device, the app warns you.

marks.title: What the marks mean
marks.text: “Decrypting…” — the message is still opening. “N messages unavailable” — they were sent before this device joined; the recovery key brings them back. “Beta” — encryption is still awaiting an independent review.

e2ee.notice: The server can't see this conversation's messages: they are encrypted on the members' devices. So there are no link previews or bots here, and search runs on your device only. A new device gets the old messages once you approve it from another one or enter your recovery key.
e2ee.opening: Setting up encryption on this device…
e2ee.waiting: Approve it from your old device or with the recovery key, and it joins on its own. Or read the code below to the other person: once they compare it, they can let this device in.
e2ee.waitingTitle: This device is not in the conversation yet
e2ee.failed: Couldn't set up encryption. Reload the page or try again later.
e2ee.groupHint: Messages, files and calls are encrypted on members' devices; the server can't see them. No search, link previews or bots here. Encryption is in beta.

safety.title: Encryption check
safety.hint: Compare the code with the other person in person or over another channel (a call, another messenger). If it matches, messages are encrypted for their devices and not for impostors.
safety.waitingDevice: {{name}}: a new device — {{device}} (signed in {{time}}). It was not approved from another of their devices, so it joins the conversation only if you let it in.
safety.compareDeviceCode: Compare the code by voice or in person: {{name}} sees it on that device’s screen. If it doesn’t match or you’re not sure, don’t let it in: this is how a server could slip in a device of its own.
safety.newOwnDevice: An unapproved device on your account: {{devices}}. If it wasn't you, remove it in “Settings → Devices” and change your password.
safety.keyChanged: {{name}} reset their encryption keys — for example, they lost all their devices, or someone is posing as {{name}}. Compare safety codes again: until you accept the new key, devices of {{name}} stay out of the conversation.

recovery.saveHint: If you lose all your devices, this key brings back your encrypted conversations. Keep it where you won't lose it: a password manager or on paper.
recovery.lossWarning: Without the key and your devices, old encrypted messages can't be recovered — not even by the server admin.
recovery.fileNote: Chinchi recovery key. It brings back your encrypted conversations on a new device. Don't show it to anyone.
recovery.enterHint: Enter the key you saved: this device gets the old messages and becomes approved.
recovery.invalid: That doesn't look like a recovery key — check you typed all of it.
recovery.wrong: This key doesn't match this account.
recovery.missing: Messages from before this device joined aren't available on it. Your recovery key brings them back.
recovery.notHere: The key is kept on your approved devices. If you saved it, enter it here so this device gets the old messages.
recovery.notSaved: You haven't marked the key as saved yet. Download it and keep it apart from your devices.
recovery.settingsHint: Brings back your encrypted conversations if all your devices are lost.
recovery.resetQuestion: Lost your recovery key and all your other devices?
recovery.resetText: New keys and a new recovery key are created. Old encrypted messages stay unavailable on this device, and the people you talk to will see that you reset your keys and can compare codes again. If you still have another device or your recovery key, use those instead.

approval.title: New sign-in

approval.compareHint: If the new device shows the same emoji in the same order, it's you. Otherwise press “No”.
approval.waiting: Open Chinchi on another of your devices and press “Yes” there. The emoji on both screens should match:
approval.declined: The sign-in wasn't approved. Try again or enter your recovery key.

e2ee.betaHint: Encryption has not been independently reviewed yet
e2ee.betaNotice: Encryption is in beta: it has not been independently reviewed yet. Rely on it with care for truly sensitive secrets.
